Overview
We are building a benchmark that tests how well AI agents handle real expert work in a terminal. We are hiring ML inference and serving experts to turn real, paid tasks from their jobs into expert-level Terminal-Bench challenges. Each task includes the environment, a working solution, and an automated check that proves the result is correct.
***THIS IS A TASK BASED COMPENSATION MODEL. PLEASE CHECK THE APPLICATION QUESTIONS FOR MORE DETAILS.***
Responsibilities
â¢ Design expert-level Terminal-Bench tasks that turn real, paid ML inference work from your own experience into challenges an AI agent must solve end to end.
â¢ Define the files, systems and environments each task runs on, such as model serving with streaming, so the challenge is realistic, reproducible and command-line solvable.
â¢ Write a working reference solution for every task and verify it runs end to end, sized for about 60 to 75 minutes of expert effort.
â¢ Build automated checks that objectively prove a result is correct, including cases where ML outputs go wrong silently, such as numerical drift or metric bugs.
â¢ Package tasks with Docker and Git so they are reproducible, and document the systems, tools, data and rules involved so reviewers can validate difficulty.
â¢ Iterate on tasks based on reviewer feedback and agent test runs, adjusting difficulty and fixing ambiguities so each task stays expert-level, fair and objectively gradable.
Skills/Experience
â¢ 3+ years doing ML inference or serving work hands-on (not only studying, selling or managing it), or a PhD plus active research in the subfield
â¢ Did this work in the last 3 years and can name the systems, tools, data and rules used
â¢ Trained, served or evaluated models at real scale (multi-GPU or production serving), not only notebooks or API calls
â¢ Hands-on with PyTorch or JAX internals and serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang or TensorRT-LLM
â¢ Can explain how ML results go wrong without errors (numerical drift, metric bugs) and how to catch them
â¢ Technical fluency in Python and the command line, and with files, CSV/JSON, APIs or databases
â¢ Availability to start by early November 2026 and complete tasks of about 60 to 75 minutes each
Nice-to-have
â¢ AI lab or LLM infrastructure experience
â¢ Contributions to PyTorch, vLLM or SGLang
â¢ GPU profiling experience
â¢ Docker and Git proficiency
â¢ Experience writing automated tests
Process
â¢ Task vetting instead of an interview: complete a vetting task so the client can assess your task design
â¢ Paid per task; each task takes about 60 to 75 minutes
â¢ Work is delivered task by task, with reviewer feedback on submissions
â¢ Expected start in early November 2026

b4e715d47cca0038.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Software Engineer on GitLab's Authorization team, you'll help build and maintain the system that decides what every user, token, and automated agent can access on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated. You'll work alongside experienced engineers who guide the larger design decisions, delivering well-scoped changes and growing into ownership of larger parts of the system.

Today, that work is Ruby on Rails. Roughly 400 policy classes and a catalog of about 1,900 permissions sit behind every application programming interface (API) request. You'll work on fine-grained token permissions, custom roles, and the GraphQL and representational state transfer (REST) APIs that enforce them. A single request can trigger hundreds of permission checks, so correctness and performance both matter.

You'll also contribute to moving the permission model to a new authorization stack that pairs the Rails monolith with a Rust policy engine. The engine represents access relationships and evaluates permission rules, and can run within the monolith's process or be reached through remote procedure calls using gRPC. You don't need prior Rust experience: several engineers on the team learned it for this work, and we'll support you doing the same.

Some examples of our projects:

  • Refactoring GitLab's policy layer so the same permission definitions can be evaluated by the monolith and the new authorization service
  • Extending fine-grained token permissions to more resources, with guidance from senior engineers on the design

What you'll do

  • Implement authorization changes in GitLab's Ruby on Rails monolith so permission checks allow intended access and deny unauthorized access.
  • Deliver well-scoped workstreams from feature-flagged rollout through verifying that the old and new systems produce the same results, with review and guidance from senior engineers.
  • Build and extend fine-grained permissions for tokens and roles so additional resources have permission coverage consistent with the established catalog.
  • Extend and fix authorization enforcement so GraphQL and the REST API enforce the intended permissions consistently.
  • Make incremental refactors to long-lived policy code without changing behavior for existing customers.
  • Investigate and fix reliability, performance, and security issues so affected permission checks return the expected results without regressions.
  • Work with the authentication, platform, and artificial intelligence (AI) teams to document interface contracts that keep permission checks consistent as authorization moves toward a shared service.
  • Contribute to design documents, merge requests, and code reviews so proposed changes have a documented rationale and review feedback is addressed asynchronously.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you'll bring

  • Solid experience building and maintaining production Ruby on Rails applications, typically gained over 2 to 4 years or more.
  • Hands-on experience with authorization concepts, such as role-based access control or fine-grained permissions, from work or projects.
  • A security mindset: you treat a permission bug as a security bug and consider who a change could affect before choosing an implementation.
  • Experience making careful changes to existing codebases, including incremental refactors and feature-flagged rollouts that preserve existing behavior.
  • Familiarity with GraphQL or API authorization patterns.
  • Awareness of performance, including how repeated permission checks can add up on every request.
  • Strong written communication and the ability to work effectively when most decisions happen in a document or merge request rather than a meeting.
  • Helpful, but not required: hands-on PostgreSQL experience, or experience with Rust, gRPC or Protocol Buffers, Cedar or other policy languages, Zanzibar-style authorization systems, Go, or service-oriented architecture.

We welcome transferable experience from adjacent domains such as identity, policy engines, and platform security.

About the team

We work in a fully asynchronous organization, with most decisions made in documents or merge requests rather than meetings.

GitLab's mission is to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. Our values include collaboration, results, efficiency, diversity, inclusion and belonging, iteration, and transparency. We expect all GitLab team members to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

  • Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off 
  • Team Member Resource Groups
  • Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Growth and Development Fund
  • Parental Leave

About Us

Sophos is a cybersecurity leader defending 600,000 organizations globally with an AI-driven platform and expert-led services. Sophos meets organizations wherever they are in their security maturity and grows with them to defeat cyberattacks. Its solutions combine machine learning, automation, and real-time threat intelligence with frontline human expertise from Sophos X-Ops to deliver advanced, 24/7 threat monitoring, detection, and response.

Sophos offers industry-leading managed detection and response (MDR) alongside a comprehensive portfolio of cybersecurity technologies — including endpoint, network, email, and cloud security, extended detection and response (XDR), identity threat detection and response (ITDR), and next-gen SIEM. Together with expert advisory services, these capabilities help organizations proactively reduce risk and respond faster, with the visibility and scalability needed to stay ahead of evolving threats.

Sophos goes to market with a global partner ecosystem, including Managed Service Providers (MSPs), Managed Security Service Providers (MSSPs), resellers and distributors, marketplace integrations, and cyber risk partners, giving organizations the flexibility to choose trusted relationships when securing their business. Sophos is headquartered in Oxford, U.K. More information is available at .

Role Summary

Sophos is seeking an experienced and motivated Security Operations Manager to support its Managed Detection and Response (MDR) customers. 

The successful candidate will be responsible for the operational management and effectiveness of the Security Operations Center and its personnel. This involves overseeing the day-to-day security operations and ensuring the strategic and operational mission of the MDR Team is fulfilled.

What you will do

• 
Maintain supervision over operational tasks and provide day-to-day oversight for threat analysts

• 
Oversee analysts in their investigation and response 

• 
Activities when security incidents arise to determine possible root cause and resolution  

• 
Effectively communicate information to stakeholders of all levels

• 
Demonstrate experience in network and host-based intrusion analysis, incident response processes and procedures, digital forensics and/or handling malware

• 
Acting as a lead throughout incident scenarios and provide subject matter expertise in cybersecurity incident response·

• 
Successfully executing incident handling procedures as well as direct response to cyber security incidents

• 
Maintaining current knowledge and recognition of attacker tools, tactics, and procedures to produce indicators of compromise (IOCs) that can be utilized during active and future investigations

• 
Assessing cyber threat intelligence/open source intelligence and operationalizing that information

• 
Demonstrating real-world, hands-on experience dealing with sophisticated malware and dynamic cyber threat actors

• 
Identifying current and emerging threats and application of such research

What you will bring

• 
5+ years of experience within a cybersecurity environment; experience in a leadership role is preferred

• 
Bachelor's in information technology, Computer Science, or a related field; or relevant, commensurate work experience

• 
Experience in a security operations center, or similar environment, and identifying indications of compromise or attack and responding to incidents

• 
Endpoint and network security experience required; IDS, IPS, EDR, ATP, Malware defenses and monitoring experience

• 
Threat hunting experience preferred

• 
Knowledge of common adversary tactics and techniques, e.g., obfuscation, persistence, defense evasion, etc.

• 
Knowledge of Mitre ATT&CK framework preferred

• 
Working knowledge of incident response procedures

• 
Experience with SQL query construction preferred

• 
Experience with OSQuery is a plus

• 
Experience administering and supporting Windows OS (both workstations and server) and one of the following: Apple or Linux-based operating systems (e.g. XP, Windows 7, 2003, 2008, OS X)

• 
Fundamental understanding of network traffic analysis including TCP/IP, routing, switching, protocols, etc.
